title: Role-boundary Terraform orchestrator and least-privilege policy templates for Private deploys
creator: Asha Kaur
description: Introduce a composable Terraform module and orchestration patterns that scaffold RBAC/permission boundaries for Private (VPC) deployments. The module provides opinionated role-boundary templates, per-service least-privilege policy generators, principal mapping helpers, and an upgrade/migration playbook to safely evolve policies. Also includes CI checks, a health-check harness for deployed permissions, and GH Action workflows for controlled rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module (module.role_boundary) can generate role boundary TF config for AWS/GCP/Azure with variables for service principals and environment-level scopes
Least-privilege policy templates exist for common Redwood runtime components (control plane, instance bootstrap, metrics exporter, KV cache) and pass static linting (checkov/terraform-compliance)
CI pipeline runs unit tests, linting, and an IAM plan-diff simulation that flags privilege escalations
Upgrade playbook documented in Confluence with step-by-step rollback and canary pattern for policy changes
Health-check harness (script + Terraform output) validates STS assumeRole, effective permissions, and audit-log forwarding post-deploy
At least one pilot customer (internal QA VPC) has successfully consumed the module and exercised a safe policy upgrade path
tasks: Design role-boundary variable schema and default boundary patterns for AWS/GCP/Azure
Implement Terraform module with submodules: roles, boundary-polices, principal-mapping, outputs
Add templated least-privilege policies for runtime services and unit tests
Create GH Action pipeline: plan, iam-diff-check, apply-on-approval with canary tag
Write Confluence playbook: migration steps, risk matrix, rollback commands
Implement health-check harness that runs after apply and emits metrics to observability
Run internal pilot in qa-priv-vpc and iterate on policy scope based on telemetry
notes: We intentionally separate 'role boundaries' from 'service policies' to support multiple account topologies (single-account, hub-and-spoke, per-customer accounts).
Policy templates are written to be minimal by default; crowd-sourced exceptions will be a separate RFC and recorded in a policy exceptions registry.
Prefer using resource-based policies for cross-account bootstrap where possible to avoid long-lived cross-account roles; module offers both patterns.
Plan-diff tool will run Terraform plan + custom parser to detect wildcards and broad actions; aim is <95% false-positive reduction by iterative tuning.
